Cyclic forms that survive norm completion

Written by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), September 2026, at Ultra. Not yet reviewed. Public domain (CC0).

A differential may be unbounded while the number obtained by integrating a product of differentials remains meaningful on K-theory. The useful estimate keeps the differentials fixed and bounds every coefficient inserted between them. We will construct the algebra on which such a form extends, prove its matrix functional calculus, and then establish the pairings. Cyclicity and the Hochschild differential have the conventions of Cyclic cohomology: traces, differentials and symmetry. The analytic construction is developed in [Connes 1986, Sections 1–2].

Throughout, Banach algebra norms are submultiplicative, and matrix traces are unnormalized. For a possibly nonunital algebra , write for the external unitization, with norm . We use this external unitization even if already has an identity. Its new unit is distinct from the old identity. K-theory of is relative to the scalar quotient .

4. The form reaches K-theory

Theorem 4.1. Inclusion induces an isomorphism on . On , define classes in by stable piecewise affine paths of invertible matrices; inclusion again induces an isomorphism.

Proof. For , approximate an ambient matrix idempotent by a matrix over . A contour separating the spectral parts near zero and one gives a nearby idempotent in the subalgebra by Theorem 3.1. Sufficiently close idempotents are equivalent: the element intertwines and and is close enough to one to be invertible. Hence every ambient class is represented.

For injectivity, suppose matrices give an equivalence between idempotents in the subalgebra, so , , , . Approximate them in their corners by over the subalgebra. The products and are invertible in their respective corners, by applying inverse closure to and . These inverses give a two-sided inverse to , so the equivalence already occurs in the subalgebra. Apply this after stabilization to prove injectivity for the group of virtual classes.

Given an ambient path between subalgebra endpoints, subdivide it finely and approximate its vertices in the subalgebra, keeping the endpoints. Uniform inverse bounds on the original compact path ensure that every resulting segment remains invertible. This supplies a piecewise affine path in the subalgebra and proves injectivity. Relative scalar classes are handled in the same way while retaining their scalar components.

6. Circle orientation remains visible in a reduced crossed product

Let a countable group act by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on the circle. Write and . We will use continuous functions of bounded variation, denoted .

Their Stieltjes derivatives are finite complex measures. The product rule is . One way to verify it is to sum the product increments over partitions: the discrepancy between using left and right endpoint values is bounded by the modulus of continuity of one function times the variation of the other, and tends to zero. Periodicity gives , hence integration by parts. Composition with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism preserves variation and obeys the same pullback rule for these measure differentials. Both assertions follow by transporting ordered partitions; the Stieltjes integral substitution follows first for step functions and then by uniform approximation.

Theorem 6.1. The inclusion is injective on .

Indeed , where compression to the identity group coordinate gives the contractive conditional expectation . Thus, for a fixed finite sum , (6.1) extends in its first argument to a bounded functional with norm at most .

Integration by parts and the orientation-preserving substitution give . For the cocycle equation it suffices to take three monomials. Every term is zero unless . In that case the first two terms cancel their derivative of the last coefficient, leaving The last term is . Applying to its integrand preserves the integral and changes it to , because and . It cancels the remainder. Hence is a one-trace.

For , its restriction gives . Theorem 5.3 supplies a homomorphism on the reduced crossed-product taking the image of to . Therefore no nonzero multiple of this image is zero. The circle K-theory identification follows from split evaluation at one point: its kernel is , , and positive suspension gives . The scalar positive loop is . This uses scalar Bott periodicity and the split-evaluation exact sequence.

If an element reverses orientation, conjugation sends to . In the crossed product that conjugation is inner and acts trivially on K-theory, so . The orientation hypothesis has a direct algebraic role.

Locally finite chains are the algebraic dual

Write . These are locally finite chains: every compact set meets only finitely many simplices. Boundary is well defined coefficient by coefficient, since any fixed face has only finitely many cofaces. Pair a chain with a finite-support cochain by the finite sum of their coefficients, using the fixed orientations. Then .

Lemma 7.8. This pairing induces an isomorphism The right side is the algebraic dual, with no boundedness requirement.

Proof. The algebraic dual of a direct sum of copies of is their product. Thus the displayed chain space is exactly the dual of the cochain space. Let , in degree . A cycle is a functional annihilating , so it restricts to a functional on . Boundaries annihilate , by the transpose identity.

Conversely, a functional on pulls back to one on annihilating . Extend it to by extending a vector-space basis. Its corresponding chain is closed and induces the required functional. This proves surjectivity. If a closed chain's functional vanishes on , define a functional on by . It is well defined precisely because annihilates . Extend it to . Its chain satisfies by transposition. This proves injectivity. These basis extensions are purely algebraic; no continuous dual or convergent infinite sum is being asserted.

8. A missing estimate and a reality operation

There are cyclic cocycles which pass every estimate with one variable coefficient but fail (1.3).

Example 8.1. Put The determinant is one. Define . The group cocycle equation follows by bilinearity and preservation of the wedge: Also . On the group algebra set It is a cyclic two-cocycle. The Hochschild identity is exactly the group equation. For cyclicity, under the group equation applied to , together with , gives ; rotate again to obtain the required equality.

Choose , , , and , regarded as group unitaries in the reduced C*-algebra. Formula (1.4) gives Both coefficient norms are one. The bottom-right entry of is unbounded: its positive-entry recurrence increases it strictly, and after two steps increases it by at least a fixed factor greater than one. Thus (1.3) fails for this fixed differential pair.

In contrast, for fixed group-ring , the functional is bounded in the reduced norm. Only finitely many coefficients of occur, each contractive by the regular representation, and their scalar weights are fixed. The distinction is the extra coefficient between the differentials.

On a -algebra define A cyclic cocycle is called real when . This is a convention for cochains, separate from the choice of constants making a K-theory number real.

Proposition 8.2. The operation (8.2) is a conjugate-linear involution on cyclic cocycles. Every cyclic cocycle is with both real.

Proof. Applying it twice reverses the arguments twice and uses , so it is an involution. Reversing the order of each multiplication in the Hochschild differential gives ; the first and last faces interchange and the middle face matches the reversed face , with this common sign. Reversing a cyclic rotation replaces it by its inverse, with the same . Hence cocycles and cyclicity are preserved. Finally take , . Conjugate linearity makes both fixed by .

The cycle-to-cocycle theorem, smooth Lie algebra differential calculus, and Chern normalizations are proved in the earlier lessons linked above. Lemma 7.3a proves the Schatten estimates used here; circle K-theory uses the previously fixed Bott and exact-sequence prerequisites. Weak amenability is the named external theorem used in Corollary 5.5. Proposition 7.7 gives the compact-support rational topological character relative to scalar Bott, compact projection/bundle identification and finite-pair exact sequences. Lemma 7.8 supplies the algebraic locally finite duality. The full relative simplicial differential-form Chern comparison is proved in the linked appendix and applied in Theorem 7.11 and Corollary 7.12. Modular-flow existence remains a separate prerequisite.
